h1: The 7 Best Docking Stations for Two Laptops of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven docks for a two-laptop desk, from KVM docks to Thunderbolt 4, compared on charging, monitors and switching.
summary: The AV Access 100W PD KVM dock is our best overall because it switches two laptops and charges both at 100W. The 13-in-1 KVM dock is the budget route with 4K120Hz support, and the AV Access 2 USB-C MST model adds dual HDMI. For one Dell laptop plus another machine, the Dell SD25TB4 is the business pick.
intro: A normal dock serves one laptop. The moment you want two laptops sharing a monitor and keyboard, you need either a dock with a built-in switch or a dock plus a separate KVM, and mixing them up is the most expensive mistake on this desk. A KVM dock does both jobs in one box.

We reviewed seven options on paper, ranking them on laptop inputs, per-laptop charging, monitor output, switching method and price tier. The list leans on listings and owner reports, and we included a mix of KVM docks and standard docks so you can see the difference.

products.name: AV Access Docking Station KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Laptops (100W PD)
products.verdict: Two laptop inputs with 100W charging on each.
products.description:
This AV Access dock has two laptop inputs and dual-monitor KVM switching, with 100W PD per laptop, 1G Ethernet, EDID emulation and 4K monitor support.

It ranks first because it delivers full 100W charging to both laptops and switches them in a single box. Against the 13-in-1 KVM below it, the main gain is a clearer per-laptop charge story, in the same $100-200 bracket.

Buy it if you need real 100W on both machines without a separate dock and switch. The caveat is 1G Ethernet only.
products.idealFor: Two-laptop desks needing full 100W charging on both.
products.skipIf: You need more than two displays.

products.name: KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Computers Docking Station (13-in-1, 100W PD)
products.verdict: A 13-in-1 aluminum KVM dock with 100W PD and 4K120Hz support.
products.description:
The 13-in-1 KVM dock is aluminum, supports 100W PD and outputs dual 4K60Hz or a single 4K120Hz signal. It takes USB-C plus HDMI and DisplayPort inputs and is plug and play.

It ranks second because it matches the AV Access on charging but trades some dual-monitor refresh for a single 4K120Hz option. It is in the $100-200 bracket.

Choose it for budget two-laptop setups that want 4K120Hz. The caveat is that 120Hz applies to a single display.

products.name: AV Access KVM Switch Dock 2 Monitors 2 Laptops (2 USB-C MST)
products.verdict: Two USB-C MST inputs and dual HDMI 4K output.
products.description:
This AV Access dock has a pair of USB-C MST inputs, one per laptop, plus twin HDMI 4K outputs and 60W of charging for each laptop, 1G Ethernet and EDID emulation.

It ranks third because 60W per laptop falls short of the 100W models above, which matters for power-hungry machines. Expect it in the $200 to $500 bracket.

Choose it for modest-power laptops and two HDMI monitors. The caveat is the lower charging wattage.
products.idealFor: Laptops that charge at 60W or less.

products.name: AV Access 8K KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Computers for Laptop & Desktop
products.verdict: Shared keyboard, mouse and monitor, with hotkey switching.
products.description:
The AV Access 8K KVM switches two computers, laptop and desktop compatible, with 8K-capable signal support and gigabit Ethernet. It shares keyboard, mouse and monitor, and uses hotkeys to switch.

It ranks fourth because it is a pure switch focus without the stated per-laptop charging of the docks above. Expect it in the $200 to $500 bracket.

Choose it for a laptop-plus-desktop setup sharing peripherals. The caveat is that charging details are not listed.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station (DL7400), 14-Port Triple Display with DisplayLink
products.verdict: A 14-port DisplayLink dock for three 4K60Hz monitors.
products.description:
The Anker Prime DL7400 is a 14-port dock with 140W max power and triple 4K60Hz displays via DisplayLink. It has a built-in cooling fan and smart display switching.

It ranks fifth because it serves one laptop at a time rather than switching a second one. It is the best pick here when one machine also needs three monitors. The listing falls in the $200-500 bracket.

Choose it for a two-laptop setup where one needs triple-monitor output. The caveat is that DisplayLink uses a driver.

products.name: Dell Pro Thunderbolt 4 Smart Dock SD25TB4
products.verdict: Four-display support and 130W PD, at full rate on Dell laptops.
products.description:
The Dell SD25TB4 supports four 4K displays, delivers 130W PD at full rate on Dell laptops and adds two Thunderbolt 4 ports, 2.5GbE Ethernet, Wi-Fi, two DP 1.4 ports and HDMI 2.1.

It ranks sixth because the full charge rate applies only to Dell laptops, and it is not a KVM switch. Expect it in the $200 to $500 bracket.

Choose it for a Dell laptop beside a second machine in a business setup. The caveat is the Dell-specific charging.
products.idealFor: Dell laptop users in a business setup.

products.award: Best for Mac and Windows Pair
products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 4 Dock for M4/M5 MacBook Air & Pro
products.verdict: A certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with driverless setup.
products.description:
The Plugable dock is Thunderbolt 4 certified with 100W charging, 4K HDMI dual monitor or single 6K, six USB ports, an SD reader and Ethernet. Setup is driverless.

It ranks last because it serves a single host at a time and is not a KVM. It suits a Mac-and-Windows pair where the Mac needs certified Thunderbolt 4. Expect it in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Buy it if one laptop is an M4 or M5 MacBook. The caveat is that it does not switch between laptops.
products.idealFor: A pair where the Mac needs certified Thunderbolt 4.

whatMatters.detail: A KVM dock switches monitors and peripherals between two computers. A standard dock serves one at a time. Look for 'KVM' and 'two laptops' in the title.
PD is the wattage sent to each laptop. Many laptops need 65W or more, and some want 100W. Check your charger's rating against the listing.
EDID emulation keeps your monitors recognized when you switch, so windows do not rearrange. It matters on every switch. Look for the term on the listing.
Docks differ in how many monitors they drive and at what refresh. Read the stated figure, such as dual 4K60Hz or triple 4K60Hz.
Thunderbolt docks suit Thunderbolt laptops, and DisplayLink needs a driver. Check what your laptops support.

faq.q: Can one dock charge two laptops?
faq.a: The KVM docks here list per-laptop charging, such as 100W PD on the AV Access model. Check the wattage for each machine.
They buy a standard dock and expect it to switch laptops. Only KVM docks do that.

faq.q: Is the AV Access worth it over the 13-in-1?
faq.a: If you want a clearer per-laptop 100W story, yes. The 13-in-1 adds a 4K120Hz option.

faq.q: How do I switch between laptops?
faq.a: Press the switch button or use a hotkey, depending on the model. The AV Access 8K lists hotkey switching.

faq.q: How do I avoid windows rearranging?
faq.a: Use a dock with EDID emulation, like the AV Access models. It keeps monitors recognized.

faq.q: Does the Dell dock charge non-Dell laptops?
faq.a: The listing says full 130W is at rate on Dell laptops. Other laptops may charge at a lower rate.

finalTake: The AV Access 100W KVM dock is the best choice for two laptops because it switches and charges both. The 13-in-1 KVM dock is the budget route, and the Dell SD25TB4 suits Dell business users. Match wattage to your laptops first.
